title: CNN tracking reveals irradiation-driven nanovoid size fluctuations and shrinkage in copper
summary: A convolutional neural network combined with greedy matching to detect, track and measure pre-existing nanovoids in in-situ TEM videos of irradiated copper. The analysis revealed non-monotonic, random-walk-like size fluctuations and shrinkage during irradiation; phase-field simulations were used to investigate the mechanism. Follow-up manual measurements and additional experiments confirmed the size-fluctuation observation.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for void detection, with greedy matching for tracking and migration analysis
organization: Purdue University; University of Hong Kong; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen

evidence.tested: A convolutional neural network combined with greedy matching to detect, track and measure pre-existing nanovoids in in-situ TEM videos of irradiated copper.
evidence.unknown: The source reports the finding for pre-existing nanovoids in irradiated copper and uses phase-field simulations to explain it. The observed fluctuation was additionally checked by manual measurements and experiments, but generalization to other materials or irradiation regimes is not established by this study.
evidence.ai_role: Automated defect recognition and tracking across high-volume in-situ microscopy video, making it possible to measure nanovoid evolution at scale; phase-field simulations then analyzed the observed dynamics.
